*BCBA owned and operated!*

*
Who we are

LaughLoveLive Again is a behavioral and mental health therapy provider that proffers therapy with an ABA twist. We believe that learning histories do not define your future. We believe that skills can be learned to improve learning repertoires that lead to socially significant behavior change.

*

*
What we do

We provide a combination of behavioral and mental health approaches for a variety of issues from anxiety, to developmental disorders like Autism Spectrum Disorder and other developmental disabilities and co-occurring disorders. We specialize in providing interventions for domestic violence and individuals that struggle with high instances of maladaptive and aggressive behaviors with autism spectrum disorder

*

*
How we do it

By utilizing up-to-date, empirically based practice, we create individualized treatment plans to ensure your training and therapeutic approach is right for you. Whether individualized or in a group setting, each client is special and deserves that attention. Services are provided in-home, in-office, in-community, in-school and online via Telehealth by board certified and licensed professionals who CARE

Job Description

Please read thoroughly before applying!

We are seeking an upbeat and compassionate Behavior Therapist to provide behavior-analytic services to a verbal adult on the autism spectrum in Miami, FL. The primary focus of this case is supporting the client in developing and strengthening executive functioning, adaptive functioning, independence, and other identified treatment goals. The ideal therapist will be comfortable providing regular 1:1 services to an adult client and collaborating with family members, a BCBA, and other professionals involved in the client’s care. The therapist will also be expected to work collaboratively with the BCBA to incorporate a behavior-analytic and mental health-informed approach into sessions to support the client’s overall success.

Schedule & Hours

This is an in-home case with morning hours and up to 25 approved hours per week. With potential for additional hours in the evening. The expected schedule is approximately 7:00/8:00 AM–12:00 PM. The therapist must be willing to work some Saturdays when necessary, including participation in Saturday morning trainings. Monthly case roundtable meetings will take place at 6:30 PM. Please only apply if you are available for the required schedule and able to commit to the needs of this case.

The adult client will participate in the interview process and will have the opportunity to ask questions of potential therapists.

Requirements

Compassion-focused and trauma-informed care is an important part of the services we provide. The ideal candidate must be able to provide services with compassion, patience, respect, and understanding and be willing to learn and apply trauma-informed approaches when working with the client. At least one year of experience working with adults, individuals on the Autism spectrum, or underserved populations is preferred. Candidates with a strong desire to work with these populations and a willingness to learn and complete additional training will also be considered.

Experience working with adults and individuals on the Autism spectrum is highly preferred. Bilingual communication skills in English and Spanish are preferred. Experience working with individuals who display hoarding behaviors is preferred; however, candidates who are willing to learn appropriate, trauma-informed strategies to support the client will also be considered. The therapist must be willing to learn about pervasive demand for autonomy and how it may impact the client’s engagement, independence, and response to therapeutic demands.

The therapist must be comfortable collaborating with the BCBA, family members, and other professionals involved in the client’s care and must be open to learning and applying behavioral principles. A foundational understanding of behavior-analytic principles is preferred, including familiarity with the main functions of behavior, the ABCs of behavior (Antecedent, Behavior, and Consequence), and effective strategies for building rapport and establishing a positive therapeutic relationship with a client. Additional training may be required prior to or throughout employment to ensure you have the knowledge and tools needed to provide high-quality services.

The ideal candidate will have an upbeat attitude, strong communication skills, and the ability to build rapport with clients and their families. An ABA background or a strong interest in pursuing growth within the field is preferred. An RBT credential and at least a bachelor's degree are highly desired.

Responsibilities

The Behavior Therapist will provide 1:1 behavior-analytic services in the client’s home and/or community under the supervision and guidance of a BCBA. Responsibilities include collecting data accurately and in real time, implementing the behavior intervention plan and treatment plan with fidelity, and communicating with the BCBA regarding observations, progress, barriers, or other relevant changes related to treatment.

The therapist will collaborate with the BCBA, family members, and other professionals involved in the client’s care and may assist with developing and reviewing service plans, treatment plans, behavior intervention plans, and skill-based assessments as needed throughout treatment. The therapist may also assist with documentation and reports for schools, courts, or other community agencies when necessary. Attendance at required group meetings, trainings, and monthly case roundtables is expected.

Pay

Pay is determined by experience, willingness to learn, and demonstrated proficiency in the skills acquired through training. The pay range for BCaBAs is $35–$50 per hour.

LaughLoveLive Again is a strong advocate for continuous learning and professional growth. Benefits

Paid RBT Competency Assessment: Receive coaching and training before completing your competency assessment. The experience and training gained while working with us can help you feel more confident when you are ready to take your exam. A pay increase is available upon obtaining your RBT credential.

Performance-Based Pay: Compensation is based on what you learn and how consistently and confidently you apply your skills, rather than solely on how long you have been with the company. Employees are evaluated every six months for opportunities for advancement and increased compensation. As you grow as a therapist, we hope you will grow with the company.

Career Advancement: Supervision is provided for individuals pursuing the BCaBA or BCBA credential. You will gain hands-on experience and have opportunities to learn and develop the skills needed to advance within the field.

Collaboration: You will have opportunities to participate in group meetings and trainings where team members can share ideas, discuss challenges, collaborate on client needs, and learn from one another.

Experience

An RBT or BCaBA certification through the BACB and in good standing is preferred.

Work Setting

About Company

The Victory Center, Inc. is a Florida-based, 501(c)(3) non-sectarian nonprofit corporation that provides children with autism and related disabilities with comprehensive, individualized treatment.

You work one-on-one with children at home, at school, and in the community, delivering kid-centered ABA therapy through games, play, and everyday routines. You follow the treatment plan your BCBA designed, collect data in real time on ABA Matrix, and write a clear session note before you head to your next family. Because we build your caseload around your availability and your neighborhood, your schedule works for you.

You are never on your own. Your BCBA visits your sessions every month to coach you in the moment, answer your questions, and celebrate the wins with you. • Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.
• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.

Do you communicate well with families? Do you work well both independently and as part of a team? If so, you might just be perfect for this position in ABA therapy!

• Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.

• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.
• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.
• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.
• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.

• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.

Why Work at D & M Behavioral Solutions?

• Competitive Compensation: $25 - $27 per hour, based on your experience, education, and certifications, paid biweekly by direct deposit.
• Full-Time Stability: Full-time, Monday to Friday, daytime and after-school field visits. We build your caseload around your availability and neighborhood.

A Day in the Life of a Lead Registered Behavior Technician

As a Lead RBT, you are the go-to person in the field. You run your own ABA sessions with families, and you are also the RBT other RBTs call when a program or a behavior gets tricky. You model procedures for newer technicians, cover sessions when a teammate is out, and give your BCBA a front-line read on how each case is really going.

Every month you help shadow new hires, support treatment-integrity checks, and share what you see with our Clinical Director so quality stays high across the team. You love teaching as much as you love therapy, and you take pride in watching the RBTs you mentor grow into confident clinicians.

As our Field Trainer, you also run skills refreshers, help a BCBA with annual RBT competency assessments, and help us improve how we train every new RBT.

What Would You Be Doing?

• Delivers ABA sessions with an assigned caseload under BCBA direction.
• Models procedures and gives in-the-field feedback to newer RBTs.
• Covers sessions when teammates are out and supports high-need cases.
• Helps with new-hire shadowing, treatment-integrity checks, and team trainings.
• Shares front-line observations with BCBAs and the Clinical Director.
• Completes accurate data and session notes in ABA Matrix within 24 hours.
• Maintains client confidentiality and follows D & M policies and the RBT Ethics Code.

What Do You Bring to the Role?

• Certification: Current RBT certification in good standing.
• Experience: Ten or more years of direct ABA experience for $27/hour; five or more for the lower end.
• Experience: Experience mentoring or training other RBTs.
• Transportation: Valid Florida driver license, reliable car, and auto insurance.
• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.
• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.
• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.

Are you the person other technicians ask for help? Do you give feedback in a way that builds people up? Are your data and session notes always clean and on time? Can you stay calm and lead when a session gets hard? If so, you might just be perfect for this Lead RBT position!

RBT Success Profile

• Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.
• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.
• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.
• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.
• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.
• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.
• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.
• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.
• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.
• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.
• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.
• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.
• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.

Physical Requirements

This role involves working in homes, schools, and community settings, occasionally lifting or moving up to 30 lbs., sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and engaging in active play for extended periods. Travel between client locations is required.

Who Are We?

D & M Behavioral Solutions is a South Florida ABA therapy provider serving children and families across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach. From our office in Pembroke Pines, our bilingual team delivers family-centered ABA at home, at school, and in the community, and coaches caregivers so progress continues between sessions.

We are big enough to keep your schedule full and small enough that you will know our Clinical Director by name. We believe the people who care for kids deserve care too, which is why every team member gets real supervision, a clear path to grow, and a wellness program that supports both mind and body.

D & M Behavioral Solutions of Pembroke Pines, FL is looking to hire a part-time or full-time Behavior Technician / ABA Therapist. Do you love working with kids? Would you rather help a child say their first words than ring up another sale? Are you looking for a career where no ABA experience is needed because we train you? If so, please read on!

Join us in partnering with families to carry out ABA treatment plans that build communication, social interaction, and daily living skills.

Why Work at D & M Behavioral Solutions?

• Competitive Compensation: $18 - $25 per hour, based on your experience, education, and certifications, paid biweekly by direct deposit.
• Flexible Scheduling: Afternoon shifts (2pm-7pm); morning and Saturday shifts optional. You tell us your availability and we build your caseload around it.
• Health and Wellness: Our PreventivePay wellness program gives you 24/7 virtual urgent care, unlimited virtual doctor visits, and ongoing virtual primary care, with no waiting rooms.
• Mental Health Support: Confidential counseling with licensed mental health counselors, plus unlimited wellness support groups: yoga, sleep coaching, emotional resilience, whole-body wellness coaching, therapeutic art, grief and loss, managing chronic pain, quitting nicotine, a men’s group, and parenting support for moms.
• Real Savings: Free acute medications and up to 80% off other prescriptions at 70,000+ pharmacies, and up to 60% off dental care with 263,000+ dentists, where each family member picks their own dentist.
• Tuition Discount: Through our partnership with Purdue University Global, you and your immediate family (spouse or partner, children, parents, and siblings) save 14% on any graduate program and 20% on any undergraduate program, in fields like psychology and ABA, health sciences, nursing, business, education, human services, and information technology.
• Supervision: Monthly BCBA supervision and coaching at no cost to you.
• Certification Support: A D & M BCBA completes your RBT competency assessment with you.
• Career Growth: Career path to RBT, Lead RBT, and our Student Analyst (RBT to BCBA) program.
• Mileage: Reimbursed between client locations at the current IRS rate.
• Impactful Work: Help a child say a first word, make a friend, or get through the day with more independence.

A Day in the Life of a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT)

As a Registered Behavior Technician, you play an essential role in helping our clients reach their goals. You work one-on-one with children at home, at school, and in the community, delivering kid-centered ABA therapy through games, play, and everyday routines. You follow the treatment plan your BCBA designed, collect data in real time on ABA Matrix, and write a clear session note before you head to your next family. Because we build your caseload around your availability and your neighborhood, your schedule works for you.

You are never on your own. Your BCBA visits your sessions every month to coach you in the moment, answer your questions, and celebrate the wins with you. Each day brings new challenges and new breakthroughs, like a first word, a calm transition, or a caregiver who thanks you by name, and you find real fulfillment in knowing your work changes a child’s life.

What Would You Be Doing?

• Implements individualized treatment plans under the direction of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA).
• Teaches communication, social, play, and daily living skills through play-based and naturalistic ABA.
• Collects accurate data in real time and completes session notes in ABA Matrix within 24 hours.
• Responds to challenging behavior using the strategies in the behavior plan.
• Checks in and out of every session at the point of care.
• Communicates professionally with caregivers, BCBAs, and the treatment team.
• Participates in monthly supervision and ongoing training.
• Maintains client confidentiality and follows D & M policies and the RBT Ethics Code.

What Do You Bring to the Role?

• Education: High school diploma or equivalent.
• Certification: Willingness to complete the 40-hour RBT training and certify within 180 days of hire.
• Transportation: Valid Florida driver license, reliable car, and auto insurance.
• Technology: A tablet or laptop for session notes.
• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.
• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.
• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.

Experience with children with autism is a plus, but multiple factors will be taken into consideration. Are you patient, dependable, and playful? Are you organized and attentive to detail? Do you communicate well with families? Do you work well both independently and as part of a team? If so, you might just be perfect for this position in ABA therapy!

RBT Success Profile

• Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.
• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.
• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.
• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.
• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.
• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.
• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.
• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.
• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.
• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.
• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.
• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.
• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.

Physical Requirements

This role involves working in homes, schools, and community settings, occasionally lifting or moving up to 30 lbs., sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and engaging in active play for extended periods. Travel between client locations is required.

Who Are We?

D & M Behavioral Solutions is a South Florida ABA therapy provider serving children and families across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach. From our office in Pembroke Pines, our bilingual team delivers family-centered ABA at home, at school, and in the community, and coaches caregivers so progress continues between sessions.

We are big enough to keep your schedule full and small enough that you will know our Clinical Director by name. We believe the people who care for kids deserve care too, which is why every team member gets real supervision, a clear path to grow, and a wellness program that supports both mind and body.

For more information, please visit www.dmbehavioralsolutions.com.

About Company

The Victory Center, Inc. is a Florida-based, 501(c)(3) non-sectarian nonprofit corporation that provides children with autism and related disabilities with comprehensive, individualized treatment.

We focus on comprehensive individualized programs with a 1:1, 2:1, and 3:1 student/teacher ratio, in a unique classroom setting.

Full-time, Monday to Friday, with a weekly mentoring block

DM’s mission is to help children with autism and their families build the skills, confidence, and daily routines to thrive at home, at school, and in the community.

DM Behavioral Solutions of Pembroke Pines, FL is looking to hire a full-time Lead Registered Behavior Technician (RBT). Do newer RBTs already come to you for help? Are you ready to get paid for it? Do you want to help keep quality high across a whole team? If so, please read on!

Join us as the field leader who helps our RBTs deliver consistent, high-quality ABA for every family.

Why Work at DM Behavioral Solutions?

• Competitive Compensation: $23 - $27 per hour, based on your experience, education, and certifications, paid biweekly by direct deposit.

• Full-Time Stability: Full-time, Monday to Friday, with a weekly mentoring block. We build your caseload around your availability and neighborhood.

• Health and Wellness: Our PreventivePay wellness program gives you 24/7 virtual urgent care, unlimited virtual doctor visits, and ongoing virtual primary care, with no waiting rooms.

• Mental Health Support: Confidential counseling with licensed mental health counselors, plus unlimited wellness support groups: yoga, sleep coaching, emotional resilience, whole-body wellness coaching, therapeutic art, grief and loss, managing chronic pain, quitting nicotine, a men’s group, and parenting support for moms.

• Real Savings: Free acute medications and up to 80% off other prescriptions at 70,000+ pharmacies, and up to 60% off dental care with 263,000+ dentists, where each family member picks their own dentist.

• Tuition Discount: Through our partnership with Purdue University Global, you and your immediate family (spouse or partner, children, parents, and siblings) save 14% on any graduate program and 20% on any undergraduate program, in fields like psychology and ABA, health sciences, nursing, business, education, human services, and information technology.

• Full-Time Benefits: Full-time team members (30+ hours) may be eligible for health benefits.

• Leadership Time: Protected mentoring time built into your week.

• Career Growth: First in line for our Student Analyst (RBT to BCBA) program and BCaBA openings.

• Mileage: Reimbursed between client locations at the current IRS rate.

• Impactful Work: Help a child say a first word, make a friend, or get through the day with more independence.

A Day in the Life of a Lead Registered Behavior Technician

As a Lead RBT, you are the go-to person in the field. You run your own ABA sessions with families, and you are also the RBT other RBTs call when a program or a behavior gets tricky. You model procedures for newer technicians, cover sessions when a teammate is out, and give your BCBA a front-line read on how each case is really going.

Every month you help shadow new hires, support treatment-integrity checks, and share what you see with our Clinical Director so quality stays high across the team. You love teaching as much as you love therapy, and you take pride in watching the RBTs you mentor grow into confident clinicians.

What Would You Be Doing?

• Delivers ABA sessions with an assigned caseload under BCBA direction.

• Models procedures and gives in-the-field feedback to newer RBTs.

• Covers sessions when teammates are out and supports high-need cases.

• Helps with new-hire shadowing, treatment-integrity checks, and team trainings.

• Shares front-line observations with BCBAs and the Clinical Director.

• Completes accurate data and session notes in ABA Matrix within 24 hours (48 hours at most).

• Maintains client confidentiality and follows DM policies and the RBT Ethics Code.

What Do You Bring to the Role?

• Certification: Current RBT certification in good standing.

• Experience: Five or more years of direct ABA experience (ten or more years for the top of the pay range).

• Experience: Experience mentoring or training other RBTs.

• Transportation: Valid Florida driver license, reliable car, and auto insurance.

• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.

• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.

• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.

Are you the person other technicians ask for help? Do you give feedback in a way that builds people up? Are your data and session notes always clean and on time? Can you stay calm and lead when a session gets hard? If so, you might just be perfect for this Lead RBT position!

RBT Success Profile

• Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.

• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.

• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.

• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.

• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.

• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.

• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.

• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.

• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.

• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.

• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.

• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.

• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.

Physical Requirements:

This role involves working in homes, schools, and community settings, occasionally lifting or moving up to 30 lbs., sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and engaging in active play for extended periods. Travel between client locations is required.

Who Are We?

DM Behavioral Solutions is a South Florida ABA therapy provider serving children and families across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach. From our office in Pembroke Pines, our bilingual team delivers family-centered ABA at home, at school, and in the community, and coaches caregivers so progress continues between sessions.

We are big enough to keep your schedule full and small enough that you will know our Clinical Director by name. We believe the people who care for kids deserve care too, which is why every team member gets real supervision, a clear path to grow, and a wellness program that supports both mind and body.

For more information, please visit www.dmbehavioralsolutions.com.

Ready to Join Our Team?

A Day in the Life of a Lead Registered Behavior Technician

As a Lead RBT, you are the go-to person in the field. You run your own ABA sessions with families, and you are also the RBT other RBTs call when a program or a behavior gets tricky. You model procedures for newer technicians, cover sessions when a teammate is out, and give your BCBA a front-line read on how each case is really going.

Every month you help shadow new hires, support treatment-integrity checks, and share what you see with our Clinical Director so quality stays high across the team. You love teaching as much as you love therapy, and you take pride in watching the RBTs you mentor grow into confident clinicians.

What Do You Bring to the Role?

• Certification: Current RBT certification in good standing.

• Experience: Five or more years of direct ABA experience (ten or more years for the top of the pay range).

• Experience: Experience mentoring or training other RBTs.

• Transportation: Valid Florida driver license, reliable car, and auto insurance.

• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.

• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.

• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.

RBT Success Profile

• Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.

• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.

• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.

• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.

• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.

• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.

• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.

• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.

• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.

• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.

• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.

• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.

• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.

Physical Requirements:

This role involves working in homes, schools, and community settings, occasionally lifting or moving up to 30 lbs., sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and engaging in active play for extended periods. Travel between client locations is required.

DM Behavioral Solutions is a South Florida ABA therapy provider serving children and families across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach. From our office in Pembroke Pines, our bilingual team delivers family-centered ABA at home, at school, and in the community, and coaches caregivers so progress continues between sessions.

For more information, please visit www.dmbehavioralsolutions.com.

Ready to Join Our Team?
